candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 19 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 20 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 21 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 22 not required. 23

candidates.context: Serious or life-threatening manifestations primarily affect children 93 Of note, section 529 describes the pediatric population as from birth through 18 years. 11 This 94 age range differs from how FDA defines the pediatric population in other contexts. Generally, 95 for drug and biological products, FDA considers the pediatric population to include patients from 96 birth through 16 years. 12 This guidance uses the term “children” to mean the definition of the 97 pediatric population in section 529: individuals aged from birth to 18 years. 98

candidates.statement: FDA interprets the current definition of “rare pediatric disease” and its reference to “serious or 100 life-threatening manifestations of the disease or condition” using the following principles: 101 • A manifestation of the disease or condition should be serious or life-threatening in 102 children aged 0 through 18 years of age. Manifestations include expressions and 103 symptoms of the disease or condition. Note that “manifestations” does not mean the 104 onset of the disease or condition or the onset of treatment. For example, if a disease or 105 condition’s onset typically begins in childhood, but manifestations of the disease or 106 condition do not become serious or life-threatening until adulthood, the disease or 107 condition is not a rare pediatric disease. Similarly, if treatment for the disease or 108 condition begins in childhood, but under current standard of care the manifestations of 109 the disease or condition are not serious or life-threatening in children, the disease or 110 condition is not a rare pediatric disease. 111 • FDA will consider the manifestations of the disease or condition in the context of 112 standard of care for the disease or condition. Specifically, FDA will consider what 113 manifestations of the disease or condition are serious or life-threatening in children under 114 standard treatment for the disease or condition. Therefore, FDA will not consider the 115 serious or life-threatening manifestations of the disease or condition that only occur when 116 the disease is left untreated if that is not the standard of care. 117 • FDA will assess the serious or life-threatening manifestations of the disease or condition 118

candidates.statement: 13 That is not to say that manifestations that primarily affect adults cannot also be serious or life-threatening in children. But based on the statutory definition, FDA is required to determine which manifestations primarily affect children and which primarily affect adults. For example, FDA has determined that impaired lung function is a serious or life-threatening manifestation of cystic fibrosis that primarily affects adults, but can also be serious or life- threatening in children. FDA considers cystic fibrosis to be a rare pediatric disease based on other manifestations of the disease that do primarily affect children.

Rare disease or condition 130 Section 526 of the FD&C Act defines a “rare disease or condition” as any disease or condition 131 that affects (1) less than 200,000 persons in the United States (U.S.) or (2) affects more than 132 200,000 in the U.S. and for which there is no reasonable expectation that the cost of developing 133 and making available in the U.S. a drug for such disease or condition will be recovered from 134 sales in the U.S. of such drug. 135

candidates.statement: A drug may also meet the “rare disease or condition” requirement if it is for an “orphan subset” 137 of a disease or condition that otherwise affects 200,000 or more persons in the U.S. 14 In order 138 for such drug to qualify as a drug for a “rare pediatric disease,” the orphan subset must be serious 139 or life-threatening and the serious or life-threatening manifestations of the orphan subset must 140 primarily affect individuals aged from birth to 18 years. 15 141

candidates.statement: • For therapeutic drugs , prevalence estimates of the entire affected U.S. population 146 should be based on the number of individuals diagnosed with the disease or condition. 147 For some diseases and conditions, individuals may have an underlying genetic 148 abnormality at birth but may not develop manifestations of the disease until later, if 149 ever. In these instances, whether individuals are considered “diagnosed” for the 150 purpose of estimating prevalence may depend on whether the product is intended to 151 treat an underlying genetic abnormality, attenuate or prevent progression of the 152 clinical expression of the disease, or treat the clinical symptoms or manifestations of 153 the disease. 154 • For vaccines, diagnostic drugs, and preventive drugs , prevalence estimates should be 155 based on the number of persons of all ages to whom the drug will be administered in 156 the U.S. annually. 157

candidates.statement: To be eligible for a voucher, the drug should be (1) approved for a rare pediatric disease and (2) 195 treat or prevent a serious or life-threatening manifestation of the disease or condition that affects 196 children. These serious or life-threatening manifestations may be the manifestations that 197 primarily affect children, but they are not required to be, so long as the approved indication is 198 clinically meaningful to pediatric patients with the disease or condition. For example: 199 • A drug may meet this standard if the approved indication is explicitly for treatment or 200 prevention of a serious or life-threatening manifestation of the disease or condition that 201 affects children. 202 • A drug may also meet this standard if the drug treats or prevents the underlying cause of 203 the disease or condition and the approved indication is for treatment or prevention of the 204 disease or condition generally. 205

candidates.statement: Clinical Trial Design – Clinical Trials for a Potential Rare Pediatric Disease Product May Need 268 to Include Individuals Over 18 Years of Age for Scientific or Ethical Reasons: Clinical trials for 269 rare diseases and conditions are challenging because, among other factors, the small patient 270 populations limit the opportunities for study and verification of results. Because such clinical 271 trials are likely to be small and at risk of being underpowered, FDA expects that rare disease 272 clinical development programs will attempt to include all patients with the rare disease or 273 condition that are available for study and who could reasonably be expected to benefit from the 274 intervention, regardless of the age of the patient (where feasible and appropriate based on the 275 disease/condition and expected effects of intervention). 24 Indeed, studies using novel therapies 276 should generally be conducted in young adults (18 to 21 years of age) prior to exposing 277
candidates.context: Thus, under this interpretation, an applicant can preserve voucher eligibility even if the applicant 261 seeks approval for use by adults in addition to pediatric patients with the rare pediatric disease. 262 One reason we are interpreting the statute in this way is to avoid incentivizing sponsors to 263 exclude adults affected by the rare pediatric disease from clinical trials or to exclude adult data 264 from the subsequent marketing application solely for the sake of voucher eligibility, when such 265 exclusions may not be scientifically or ethically acceptable for the reasons described below. 266 24 See, e.g., ICH and FDA Guidance, “E11 Clinical Investigation of Medicinal Products in the Pediatric Population,” Section II.A, available at http://www.fda.gov/downloads/RegulatoryInformation/Guidances/ucm129477.pdf .
